data.name: proposal
data.source: app.describeArchiveStrategy.execute — a confirmation minted against BattleGrid's own count of bound agents; the consequence wording is the wording stored with the token

data.name: listing
data.source: app.listStrategies.execute — the roster read that locates the strategy; its failure is a distinct page state

data.name: problem
data.source: searchParams — the reason a rejected archiveStrategy redirected back with. Three producers now: a platform `refused`, a platform `repair-required`, and — since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` — the action's own pre-perform re-read failing or the strategy having left the roster, both of which arrive prefixed 'Nothing was attempted: …'

components.purpose: Ask one question — archive this strategy? — with what depends on it stated, in BattleGrid's words, before the button.
components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centered column, space-y-4, p-6 — the confirmation-page skeleton, deliberately following the agent archive page rather than inventing a second shape. Four post-connection branches, and since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` all four mount `<CarriedProblem>` unconditionally as the first thing under the h1 — it renders null when there is no carried reason, so every `-with-problem` pairing above is a real rendering rather than a variant somebody has to remember. Since DT-0019 landed, this page's own two failure sentences wear the danger role rather than body text: `refused` renders h1 'Cannot archive <name>' plus the platform's reason as `rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary` with role=alert, and a plain underlined link back — no form, nothing styled as though retrying could help. `unreadable` is the roster read failing: the reason in the same danger block, then WhyNotLoaded's reassurance as a separate plain `mt-2` paragraph *beneath* the block rather than inside it (worth stating plainly: the tinted block holds only the platform's sentence), and the way out is the roster ('Back to your strategies'), not the strategy — the read that would have said the strategy is there is the one that failed. `no-such-strategy` stays deliberately plain — a bare h1 and the same roster link, no reason paragraph at all, because a strategy that is not in the list is an answer rather than a failure. Note what the `-with-problem` pairings mean visually now that both blocks are tinted: on `unreadable` and `refused` two danger blocks stack — the carried reason for the click that bounced, then this page's own fresh failure — identical in treatment and different in fact, separated only by the carried banner's semibold 'Refused: ' prefix and the gap between them.
constraints: Every branch renders the carried reason, not just the ones that can offer a form — the branch that drops it loses the only record of what the click did, and `tests/agent/refusals-reach-the-operator.test.ts` asserts one `<CarriedProblem>` per `<main>` on this page. A design that suppresses it on a terminal branch changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

Where two danger blocks stack (carried reason above this page's own failure reason), both must stay readable as separate claims — collapsing them into one block would merge 'your archive was refused' with 'the roster would not load'. They now share one treatment by DT-0019's decision, so whatever keeps them separable is doing the whole job.

Before archiving, the page states what is bound to the strategy — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:237 ('Grid-Commander SHALL state, before a strategy is archived, what is bound to it') and spec.md:245-248 ('they are first told how many agents are bound to it … archiving is described as reversible'). The consequence block is where both live; a design must keep it before the buttons.
The page renders whole from one server round trip — no client JS, no hydration. A design requiring client-side interactivity changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.
The refused and unreadable reason paragraphs keep role=alert, and keep the danger treatment DT-0019 landed — a design that returns either of them to body text undoes a decided ruling.
`no-such-strategy` stays plain prose — it carries no reason paragraph at all, and DT-0019 ruled that deliberate: an answer is not a failure and must not be tinted as one.
WhyNotLoaded's reassurance must survive verbatim wherever it renders relative to the danger block — the tint says something failed; only those words say what did not.
'Nothing is styled to look disabled when retrying cannot help' (system.json principle) — the refused state offers no form and must stay that way.

components.purpose: Show the reason that bounced a submitted archive back to the person who clicked it — whether the platform refused it or nothing was attempted at all.
components.current_implementation: The shared `CarriedProblem` component (src/presentation/components/carried-problem.tsx), extracted by `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` from the copy that used to be inline on this page. Carries DT-0004's danger treatment unchanged — rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert, opening with a semibold 'Refused: ' prefix so the state is named as well as tinted — and returns null for a falsy `problem`, which is what lets every branch mount it unconditionally. Its prop now takes `string | null | undefined` (widened by `a-lost-authority-is-not-a-refusal` so callers reading a parsed query, which yields null, are not tempted to hand-roll their own copy); nothing about its rendering changed. DT-0019 gave this page's own failure sentences the same treatment, so the banner is no longer the only tinted block on the page — it is distinguished by the 'Refused: ' prefix, not by its palette.
constraints: role=alert must survive.

The reason is BattleGrid's, verbatim — `repair-required` refusals arrive through the same channel and the wording must survive whatever the platform sends. The action's own 'Nothing was attempted: …' sentences ride the same field and take the same treatment.
This is a failed attempt, not advisory — it may take a stronger role than the consequence block, but 'notice never borrows danger's colour' (system.json principle) binds the blocks beside it.

Shared by six ceremony pages (agent deploy/undeploy/rebind, strategy archive/restore/fork) — restyle it in the component, never per page, or the six renderings of one paragraph drift the way they did before it was extracted.
The 'Refused: ' prefix is part of the treatment even when the sentence that follows says nothing was attempted — a design may restyle the prefix but must not drop the naming of the state.

components.purpose: State what archiving does and what is bound to the strategy — BattleGrid's count, not ours — before the button that does it.
components.current_implementation: rounded-gc-2 border border-border-default p-4 text-sm with role=alert — a plain border, NOT the consequence-border/bg-consequence-subtle treatment DT-0004 gave the agent ceremony pages, and now the only bordered block on this page that is not tinted, since DT-0019 gave the failure sentences danger. The sentence is the platform's, verbatim, and is the same string stored with the confirmation token.
constraints: The text is the wording the confirmation token was minted against — a design must not paraphrase, truncate, or summarize it; what the user reads, what they agree to, and what the audit can prove are one string.
Consequence outranks everything on a screen (system.json principle) — this block must not become lighter than the buttons below it.
role=alert must survive.
Archiving is recoverable and must not be described or styled as deletion — spec.md:248 ('archiving is described as reversible').

components.purpose: Reassure someone staring at a failed read that their strategy still exists, by naming the accurate external cause.
components.current_implementation: Shared WhyNotLoaded component (why-not-loaded.tsx), rendered only in the unreadable state: one plain `mt-2` paragraph — 'This does not mean this strategy is gone —', completed by the cause (authority refused vs. platform unreachable). It renders as a sibling *after* the danger block DT-0019 landed, not inside it; the component itself was untouched by that ticket. Shared across every read-failure surface so the wording cannot drift.
constraints: The two causes must stay distinguishable — a 401 is not an outage, and telling someone with a bad credential to wait for an outage is the dangerous half to get wrong (the component's own history).
The reassurance sentence is the point and must not be cut for space.

components.purpose: Carry the archive decision: one committing button, one visible way out.

actions.effect: POSTs the server action with strategyId and confirmationToken; success lands on /strategies, refusal (refused and repair-required both) redirects back here with ?problem=, and a pre-perform re-read that fails or a strategy that has left the roster also redirects back here with ?problem= prefixed 'Nothing was attempted: …'

components.current_implementation: flex flex-wrap gap-3 — buttons wrap rather than stacking; there is no w-full/tablet:w-auto mobile stack here, unlike the agent ceremony pages. Two hidden inputs carry the confirmation binding (strategyId, confirmationToken — no expectedRevision travels; staleness is the token's to enforce). Since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` the action reads its own re-read: an unreadable roster and a strategy no longer in it each bounce back to this route with a 'Nothing was attempted: …' problem, where they used to redirect to /strategies unexplained.
constraints: A click that reached no operation still lands somewhere that says so — the two 'Nothing was attempted: …' paths must not be redesigned back into a silent redirect to the roster.
The hidden binding (strategyId, confirmationToken) is the confirmation ceremony — the form must keep exactly one submit path.
Cancel must remain a visible peer of the submit, never a text link beneath it (DT-0002 ruling, restated in control.ts).
Declining returns to the strategy, not the list — spec.md:240-243 ('Declining SHALL return the user to what they were looking at').

components.purpose: Commit the archive. Named with the strategy: 'Archive <name>'.
components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY constant from control.ts — accent.default bg, min-h-control (size.control.min, 44px, tokenised by DT-0003), rounded-gc-2, hover to accent.hover over duration-fast, active holds hover at duration-instant. No pending/loading state between click and redirect — the same class of gap filed as #153 for the agent archive button; behavior, not styling. DT-0022 added the primitive's `disabled` treatment to this constant — bg.sunken ground, text.disabled label, border.subtle edge and cursor not-allowed, stated rather than an opacity. DT-0022 defined the primitive's `disabled` treatment on this constant, but **nothing in the product enters it** — so it is not listed as a state of this surface. system.json declares it and DT-0022 styles it; a surface claiming a state it cannot reach is the same fiction DT-0003 refused for the ghost and danger variants.
constraints: Deliberately NOT danger-styled — DT-0002's ruling, restated in control.ts: archive is the legitimate action; the weight belongs on the consequence block. A design ticket restyling this as danger contradicts a decided ruling.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_PRIMARY constant in control.ts, shared by every committing submit in the product — not a per-page className.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
Focus ring comes from the one global rule in globals.css — do not add a per-element ring.

components.purpose: Leave the strategy active and go back to it — to the strategy, not the list, so declining costs nothing.
components.current_implementation: An anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — inline-flex centering, min-h-control, DT-0004 hover (border-border-strong + bg-bg-sunken over duration-fast; active holds it at duration-instant). Label 'Leave it active'.
constraints: Must remain an anchor (pure navigation, no form participation) and must remain a visible peer of the submit.
Must keep pointing at the strategy, not the roster — spec.md:250-252 ('they are returned to the strategy rather than to the list'); sending them to the list makes the safe choice the more costly one.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_SECONDARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).

components.purpose: Turn away a request without authority, with the one remedy that works: connect.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, and since DT-0006 the connect link is an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — the way in as a target, not a sentence, at the 44px floor with secondary's hover. Used by every authenticated page, so this treatment is inherited everywhere.
constraints: Every no-authority cause renders this same page by design (see design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants.

flows.name: Archive a strategy
steps: read what is bound to it in BattleGrid's words
land on /strategies with the strategy retired

flows.name: Archive is refused after submit
steps: platform refuses (revision moved, not permitted, repair-required)
problem banner states the reason above the still-usable form

flows.name: Nothing could be attempted
steps: the action's re-read of the roster fails, or the strategy is no longer in it
redirected back here with ?problem= 'Nothing was attempted: …'
whichever branch renders next carries that sentence — including the branch reporting its own fresh read failure

flows.name: Archive cannot even be described
steps: describe is refused before any form renders
one link back to the strategy; no form offered
a carried reason, if one rode in, sits above that reason

accessibility.notes: The carried problem (shared CarriedProblem, present on all four branches), the consequence, and the refused/unreadable reasons all carry role=alert — so a branch that reports its own failure with a reason riding in announces two alerts, deliberately. Since DT-0019 the two failure alerts are visually identical as well, which puts the whole burden of telling them apart on wording and order. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). No client JS: every state change is a full navigation, so the alerts are read in document order rather than as live-region updates.
